info.title: Edgee API
info.description: Edgee is an edge-native AI Gateway with private model hosting, automatic model selection, cost audits/alerts, and edge tools. This API is OpenAI-compatible, providing one API for any model and any provider.

post.description: Creates a completion for the chat message. Supports both streaming and non-streaming responses. The API is OpenAI-compatible and works with any model and provider.

schema.description: Server-Sent Events stream. Each event is a JSON object prefixed with 'data: ' and followed by two newlines. Each event has a `type` field. Text responses produce: `response.created`, `response.output_item.added`, `response.content_part.added`, `response.output_text.delta`, `response.output_text.done`, `response.content_part.done`, `response.output_item.done`, `response.completed`. Tool calls additionally produce: `response.function_call_arguments.delta`, `response.function_call_arguments.done`.

post.description:
Estimates the number of input tokens for a request shaped like the Anthropic [Messages API](#tag/Messages). Always forwards to the Anthropic provider's tokenizer. Returns an `input_tokens` count compatible with `/v1/count_tokens`.

**Note:** `max_tokens` is accepted but ignored by this endpoint.

post.description:
Compresses an LLM request payload and returns it with the `messages`, `input`, `system`, and `tools` fields replaced by their compressed versions. Accepts OpenAI Chat Completions, Anthropic Messages, and OpenAI Responses API formats — the wire format is auto-detected from the request body.

No LLM provider is called. This is a pure pre-processing step intended for teams running their own LLM gateways who want Edgee token compression without routing requests through Edgee.

post.description:
Estimates the number of input tokens for a set of messages without making an LLM call. Accepts both OpenAI chat format and Anthropic Messages format, the format is auto-detected from the message structure. Useful for pre-flight cost estimation, rate-limit planning, and prompt optimization.

**Note:** Token counts are approximate and may differ from provider-native tokenizers (e.g. OpenAI tiktoken, Anthropic's tokenizer).

401.description: Unauthorized - missing or invalid API key

model.description: ID of the target model. Format: `{author_id}/{model_id}`. The gateway uses this to pick the appropriate tokenizer when `tokenizer` is not provided.

messages.description: Optional array of message objects to count tokens for. Accepts both OpenAI chat format (with `system`, `user`, `assistant` roles) and Anthropic Messages format; the format is auto-detected from the message structure. Defaults to an empty array.

role.description: The role of the message author.

content.description: The message content. Can be a plain string or an array of content blocks.

system.description: Optional system prompt. Accepts a plain string or an array of Anthropic content blocks. Used when counting tokens for an Anthropic-style request.

tokenizer.description: Explicit tokenizer override. When omitted, the gateway picks one based on `model`.

input_tokens.description: Estimated number of input tokens for the provided messages. This is an approximation, counts may differ from provider-native tokenizers. Use for estimation and budgeting, not exact billing.

model.description: ID of the model to use. Format: `{author_id}/{model_id}` (e.g. `openai/gpt-5.2`)

messages.description: A list of messages comprising the conversation so far.

max_tokens.description: The maximum number of tokens that can be generated in the chat completion.

stream.description: If set, partial message deltas will be sent, as in OpenAI. Streamed chunks are sent as Server-Sent Events (SSE).

include_usage.description: If set, an additional `[DONE]` message will be sent with usage statistics when the stream is finished.

tools.description: A list of tools the model may call. Currently, only `function` type is supported.

oneOf.description: Bare-string mode. `none` forbids tool calls; `auto` lets the model decide.

tool_choice.description: Controls which tool (if any) the model is allowed to call. Accepts a bare string (`none` / `auto`), a typed-mode object (`{ "type": "auto" | "none" }`), or a specific function reference.

edgee_tool_ids.description: List of Edge Tool IDs to inject (e.g. edgee_current_time, edgee_generate_uuid). Each ID must be activated for your API key. When omitted or empty, only tools with hydration enabled for your org or API key are auto-injected. Invalid or non-activated IDs return 400 with invalid_edgee_tool_ids.

edgee_pending_id.description: Pending operation ID when continuing a conversation after Edge Tool execution (e.g. when mixing client-side and Edge Tools). The gateway injects stored Edge Tool results into the message history.

tags.description: Optional tags to categorize and label the request. Useful for filtering and grouping requests in analytics and logs. Can also be sent via the `x-edgee-tags` header as a comma-separated string.

enable_debug.description: When `true`, the response includes additional debug information. Equivalent to the `X-Edgee-Debug` header.

ToolChoiceTypedMode.description: Typed-mode form of `tool_choice` — an object containing only a `type` field set to `auto` or `none`.

CompressionModel.description: Selects the compression bundle to apply to the request. Equivalent to the `X-Edgee-Compression-Model` header.

role.description:
The role of the message author. Required properties vary by role:
- `system`, `user`, `developer`: requires `content`
- `assistant`: `content` is optional (can be empty if `tool_calls` is present)
- `tool`: requires `content` and `tool_call_id`

content.description: The contents of the message. Required for all roles except `assistant` (where it can be empty if `tool_calls` is present). For `assistant` role, defaults to empty string if not provided.

name.description: An optional name for the participant. Provides the model information to differentiate between participants of the same role. Used for `system`, `user`, `assistant`, and `developer` roles.

tool_call_id.description: The ID of the tool call that this message is responding to. Required for `tool` role only.

refusal.description: The refusal message from the model, if any. Used for `assistant` role only.

tool_calls.description: The tool calls made by the assistant. Used for `assistant` role only.

cache_control.description: Anthropic prompt-cache control passthrough. Applied when routing to an Anthropic-backed model. Used on `system`, `user`, and `assistant` roles only.

type.description: The type of the tool. Currently, only `function` is supported.

name.description: The name of the function to be called. Must be a-z, A-Z, 0-9, or contain underscores and dashes, with a maximum length of 64.

description.description: A description of what the function does, used by the model to choose when and how to call the function.

parameters.description: The parameters the functions accepts, described as a JSON Schema object. See the guide for examples, and the JSON Schema reference for documentation about the format.

name.description: The name of the function to call.

id.description: The ID of the tool call.

type.description: The type of the tool call.

name.description: The name of the function to call.

arguments.description: The arguments to call the function with, as JSON.

id.description: A unique identifier for the chat completion.

object.description: The object type, which is always `chat.completion`.

created.description: The Unix timestamp (in seconds) of when the chat completion was created.

model.description: The model used for the chat completion.

choices.description: A list of chat completion choices. Can be more than one if n is greater than 1.

edgee_pending_id.description: Present when one or more Edge Tool calls were deferred. Pass this value back as `edgee_pending_id` in the next request to resume the conversation with the tool results filled in.

edgee_tools_executed.description: List of Edge Tools the gateway executed inline before returning. Empty or absent when no Edge Tools ran.

EdgeeToolExecuted.description: Summary of an Edge Tool that was executed inline by the gateway.

index.description: The index of the choice in the list of choices.

finish_reason.description: The reason the model stopped generating tokens. This will be `stop` if the model hit a natural stop point or a provided stop sequence, `length` if the maximum number of tokens specified in the request was reached, `content_filter` if content was omitted due to a flag from our content filters, or `tool_calls` if the model called a tool.

Usage.description: Usage statistics for the completion. In streaming responses, this is only present in the final chunk when `stream_options.include_usage` is true.

prompt_tokens.description: Number of tokens in the prompt.

completion_tokens.description: Number of tokens in the generated completion.

total_tokens.description: Total number of tokens used in the request (prompt + completion).

cached_tokens.description: Number of cached tokens read from the prompt cache.

cache_creation_tokens.description: Number of tokens written to the prompt cache (Anthropic-style cache creation).

reasoning_tokens.description: Number of reasoning tokens in the output.

object.description: The object type, which is always `list`.

id.description: The model identifier, which can be referenced in the API. Format: `{author_id}/{model_id}`.

object.description: The object type, which is always `model`.

created.description: The Unix timestamp (in seconds) when the model was created.

owned_by.description: The organization that owns the model.

ChatCompletionChunk.description: A streaming chunk in the chat completion response. Used when `stream: true` in the request.

id.description: A unique identifier for the chat completion chunk.

object.description: The object type, which is always `chat.completion.chunk` for streaming responses.

created.description: The Unix timestamp (in seconds) of when the chat completion was created.

model.description: The model used for the chat completion.

choices.description: A list of chat completion choices for this chunk.

ChatCompletionChunkChoice.description: A choice in a streaming chat completion chunk.

index.description: The index of the choice in the list of choices.

delta.description: A delta representing the change in the message content. The first chunk typically contains `role`, subsequent chunks contain `content`.

finish_reason.description: The reason the model stopped generating tokens. This will be `null` for all chunks except the final one. This will be `stop` if the model hit a natural stop point or a provided stop sequence, `length` if the maximum number of tokens specified in the request was reached, `content_filter` if content was omitted due to a flag from our content filters, or `tool_calls` if the model called a tool.

Delta.description: Represents a change in message content. The first chunk typically contains `role`, subsequent chunks contain `content`.

role.description: The role of the message author. Typically present only in the first chunk.

content.description: The content of the message delta. Present in content chunks.

ErrorResponse.description: Error response. The `error` object follows OpenAI's error envelope shape; the gateway additionally populates `type` (Anthropic-style category) and `param` when applicable.

type.description: Anthropic-style high-level error category. Always present.

code.description: A machine-readable error code. Currently emitted values: `unauthorized`, `forbidden`, `invalid_json`, `bad_model_id`, `model_not_found`, `provider_not_supported`, `invalid_tokenizer`, `invalid_request`, `usage_limit_exceeded`, `provider_error`, `internal_error`.

param.description: Name of the request parameter that caused the error, when applicable.

model.description: The model ID to use (Anthropic format, without provider prefix)

max_tokens.description: Maximum number of tokens to generate

description.description: Description of what the tool does

input_schema.description: JSON Schema describing the tool's input parameters

type.description: Model decides whether to use tools
Model must use one of the provided tools

name.description: Name of the specific tool to use

model.description: The model that generated the response

CompressionInfo.description: Token compression metrics. Present in the response when token compression was applied to the request. The `usage.prompt_tokens` field reflects the compressed token count actually billed by the provider.

saved_tokens.description: Number of input tokens saved by compression (original count minus compressed count).

cost_savings.description: Estimated cost savings in micro-units. Divide by `1000000` to convert to USD. Example: `27000` = $0.027 saved.

reduction.description: Percentage reduction in input tokens. For example, `48` means the compressed prompt was 48% smaller than the original.

time_ms.description: Time taken to perform compression, in milliseconds.

cache_read_input_tokens.description: Number of input tokens read from the prompt cache.

cache_creation_input_tokens.description: Number of input tokens written to the prompt cache.

model.description: ID of the model to use, with provider prefix. Format: `{author_id}/{model_id}`.

input.description: The input to the model. Either a plain string (treated as a single user message) or a flat array of typed input items (messages, function calls, function call outputs).

instructions.description: System-level instruction prepended to the conversation. An alternative to including a `system` role message in the `input` array.

stream.description: If set, the response is streamed as Server-Sent Events (SSE).

max_output_tokens.description: Maximum number of tokens to generate.

tools.description: Tools available to the model. Uses the Responses API flat format (no nested `function` key).

oneOf.description: Bare-string mode. `auto` lets the model decide; `none` forbids tool calls.

temperature.description: Sampling temperature between 0 and 2. Higher values produce more random outputs.

top_p.description: Nucleus sampling probability. Alternative to temperature.

tags.description: List of string tags for categorizing and filtering requests in analytics and logs. Can also be sent via the `X-Edgee-Tags` header.

enable_debug.description: Enable debug mode to include additional information in the response.

edgee_tool_ids.description: List of Edgee-managed tool IDs to include automatically (e.g. `edgee_current_time`, `edgee_generate_uuid`). Each ID must be activated for your API key.

edgee_pending_id.description: Pending operation ID when continuing a conversation after Edge Tool execution. The gateway injects stored Edge Tool results into the conversation history.

ResponsesInputItem.description: A single item in the `input` array. Either a message turn, an assistant function call, or a function call output.

role.description: The role of the message author.

content.description: Message content. Either a plain string or an array of typed content parts.

call_id.description: Identifier linking this call to its `function_call_output`.

name.description: Name of the function the assistant is calling.

arguments.description: Arguments passed to the function, encoded as a JSON string.

call_id.description: Identifier matching the `function_call` item this is responding to.

output.description: Tool result, encoded as a string (typically JSON).

ResponsesContentPart.description: A typed content part within a message item.

ResponsesTool.description: Tool definition in the Responses API flat format. Unlike Chat Completions, there is no nested `function` key.

description.description: Description of what the function does, used by the model to choose when to call it.

parameters.description: JSON Schema object describing the function's parameters.

ResponsesToolChoiceFunction.description: Forces the model to call the specified function.

name.description: Name of the function to call.

id.description: Unique identifier for the response, prefixed with `resp_`.

status.description: `completed` for non-streaming responses; `in_progress` is emitted on the initial `response.created` SSE event.

created_at.description: Unix timestamp (as a float) of when the response was created.

model.description: The model used to generate the response.

output.description: Array of output items produced by the model.

type.description: `message` for text responses, `function_call` for tool calls.

content.description: Array of content parts within this output item.

ResponsesOutputContent.description: A content part within an output item.

arguments.description: Tool call arguments as a JSON string.

ResponsesUsage.description: Token usage statistics for the response.

CompressRequest.description: An LLM request payload to compress. Accepts any of three wire formats — the format is auto-detected from the request body: a top-level `"system"` key indicates Anthropic Messages format; a top-level `"input"` key indicates OpenAI Responses API format; otherwise, OpenAI Chat Completions format is assumed.

CompressMetadata.description: Token compression metrics appended to every `/v1/compress` response.

technique.description: `auto` when all applicable strategies are tried; `tool` when a specific compression model was requested via the `X-Edgee-Compression-Model` header or `compression_model` body field.

applied_strategies.description: Names of the compression strategies that were applied to the request.

compression_rate.description: Fraction of input tokens removed (0.0–1.0). For example, `0.19` means 19% of input tokens were removed.

uncompressed_input_tokens.description: Token count of the original, uncompressed input.

compressed_input_tokens.description: Token count after compression. This is what the downstream LLM provider will be billed for.

compression_time_ms.description: Wall-clock time taken to perform compression, in milliseconds.

error.description: Human-readable error message if compression partially failed. Present only when an error occurred during compression.

tool_stats.description: Per-tool compression statistics. Present only when `tool_result_trimming` was applied.

CompressResponse.description: The original request payload with compressed content fields replaced. All fields not touched by compression (`model`, `temperature`, `top_p`, `stop_sequences`, etc.) pass through unchanged. A `compression` object is always appended.

bearerAuth.description: Bearer authentication header of the form `Bearer <token>`, where `<token>` is your API key. More info [here](/docs/api-reference/authentication)

apiKeyAuth.name: x-api-key
apiKeyAuth.description: Anthropic-style API key authentication using the x-api-key header
